---
title: Upskii production E2E
description: What the Upskii production end-to-end workflow checks, how to read a failure, the kill switch, and the cleanup guarantees.
---

The `Upskii Production E2E` workflow
(`.github/workflows/upskii-production-e2e.yaml`) runs Playwright suites
against the production hosts `tuturuuu.com`, `meet.tuturuuu.com`,
`app.upskii.com`, `upskii.com` and `admin.upskii.com`. Every account it uses is a
disposable QA identity, and it removes everything it creates, including on
failure. The hosts are fixed in code (`apps/web/e2e-upskii-production/policy.ts`),
so the suite cannot be pointed at another deployment.

## Suites

| Suite | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| `meet-flow` | Upskii sign-in; linking a Tuturuuu account (consent on the Tuturuuu login page, the callback, link state on both sides); the host starting a Meet session and presenting Upskii content; a learner's lobby, admission and Mira consent; the meeting record; unlink and sign-out. Negative cases: forged and expired link state, a cross-account callback, a link conflict, an unadmitted join, a non-member or signed-out meeting-record read, and a participant who declines Mira being excluded. |
| `educator` | Classes, invitations and membership, lessons and modules, files, assessments and grading, course quizzes, flashcards, one AI chat call, tutor sessions, announcements, and settings. Also the permission negatives: learner, outsider and signed-out callers are refused. |
| `learner` | Courses, lessons and progress, materials, assessment attempts, flashcards, notifications, grades, and every learner navigation page. Also wrong-experience and outsider refusals. |
| `admin` | Every admin API family refuses QA teachers, learners and signed-out callers, and the admin shell refuses non-admins. QA identities never hold an Upskii admin role. |

The `educator` and `learner` suites make at most one AI model call per run.

## Triggers and bounds

| Trigger | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| `workflow_dispatch` (`mode: run`, optional `suites`) | The selected suites, then cleanup |
| `workflow_dispatch` (`mode: sweep`) | Orphan cleanup only |
| `workflow_run` after a successful `Production Deployment Planner` or `Meet Cloudflare` run from the `production` branch | All suites |
| `repository_dispatch` `upskii-production-deployed`, sent by Upskii's production deploy | All suites |
| Daily schedule (20:43 UTC) | Orphan cleanup only; the suites never run on a schedule |

- **Trusted triggers only.** A credential-free `gate` job re-proves every `workflow_run` completion with the canonical trust step (producer path, workflow ID, exact branch, event, conclusion and same repository) and applies the kill switch before the production job starts.
- **One run at a time.** Runs share the concurrency group `upskii-production-e2e`, which never cancels a run that is cleaning up.
- **No retries.** Playwright retries are `0`, and production writes are not repeated.
- **Hard timeouts.** The job has 48 minutes, the suites 22, each test 120 seconds and each API request 20 seconds. Cleanup has a 5-minute deadline.
- **Daily runs.** The Tuturuuu operator allows at most 12 QA runs per rolling 24 hours. Each suite run uses two (members and the non-member), so about six suite runs a day fit.

## Kill switch

Set the repository variable `UPSKII_PRODUCTION_E2E_ENABLED` to anything other
than `true` to stop every trigger; the job is skipped. The suite code repeats
the check (`readRunConfig`), so a local or forked invocation cannot reach
production either. Cleanup-only runs (`mode: sweep`) need the switch on as well.

Two upstream switches also stop provisioning:
- `private.qa_test_user_control` for Tuturuuu QA accounts (see
  [QA test users](/build/development-tools/qa-test-users));
- `QA_PROVISIONER_ENABLED` on the Upskii Admin Worker.

## Credentials

| Name | Where | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub OIDC token, audience `https://tuturuuu.com/qa-operator` | Minted per job (`id-token: write`) | Tuturuuu QA operator. The server admits only this workflow file on `main` in environment `upskii-production-e2e`, and acts as `QA_CI_OPERATOR_USER_ID` within the CI caps. |
| `UPSKII_QA_PROVISIONER_TOKEN` | Secret in environment `upskii-production-e2e` | Upskii per-run QA identities, the seed class, and the purge |
| `UPSKII_PRODUCTION_E2E_ENABLED` | Repository variable | Kill switch |

Passwords that the provisioners return stay in a `0600` file, written
atomically, in a private `0700` directory under the runner's temp directory.
Global teardown deletes it, and `cli.ts cleanup` deletes it again in case
Playwright crashed first. Traces and video are off,
because they can capture session cookies. Failure screenshots are kept for
3 days.

## Cleanup guarantees

Cleanup works through two kinds of owner, recorded in an append-only run
ledger (`$RUNNER_TEMP/upskii-production-e2e/ledger.jsonl`) before each create call
returns:

- **A Tuturuuu QA run.** Deleting it deletes its accounts and run workspace.
  The meetings, meeting records, uploads and external account links in that
  workspace go with it.
- **An Upskii QA identity.** The admin purge hard-deletes everything the
  identity owns, then disables it. The purge refuses any account without the
  provisioner-only QA marker.

Every other object a test creates is tracked with the owner that removes it
(`coveredBy`), and the test also deletes it through the product API in a
`finally` block. The workflow runs four passes:

1. **Sweep** before the tests: removes owners that earlier runs left behind. The workflow allows only one run at a time, so every remaining suite owner is an orphan.
2. **Global teardown** (Playwright) cleans up in-process.
3. **`cli.ts cleanup`** (`if: always()`) runs again, even if Playwright crashed.
4. **`cli.ts verify`** (`if: always()`) re-reads both servers. The step fails if any owner in this ledger still exists, any tracked object has no owner, or any `upskii-e2e` QA account or run-labelled Upskii identity is still live from any run.

Every step is idempotent, so re-running a failed workflow or dispatching
`mode: sweep` is safe.

The sweep is bounded: it reads at most five provisioner pages (500 Upskii
identities) per run. Provisioning allows far fewer per day, so one sweep
normally clears everything. If more remain, the sweep and verify steps fail
and name the incomplete listing; dispatch `mode: sweep` again until verify
passes.

## Reading a failure

Failures keep one open internal alert task (key `upskii-production-e2e`, see
[CI alert tasks](/build/devops/ci-alert-tasks)). The next green run comments on
the task and resolves it. No public GitHub issue is opened.

| Failed step | Meaning | Next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Sweep orphans from earlier runs` | A provisioner or cleanup API refused or timed out | Check the provisioner switches and Tuturuuu `/api/v1/admin/qa/test-users` health; dispatch `mode: sweep` |
| `Run production suites` | A product regression or an environment change | The job summary and JUnit report name the suite and test; screenshots are in the run artifact |
| `Clean up this run` | An owner could not be deleted | Dispatch `mode: sweep`; if it keeps failing, the cleanup API is broken and needs a fix |
| `Verify nothing leaked` | Test data is still present | Treat as a release blocker for the cleanup path; the annotations list each leaked owner |

Run locally only with an operator's explicit approval: the suites write to
production. Set the same variables, then run
`bun x playwright test --config playwright.upskii-production.config.ts` from
`apps/web`. The `cli.ts` commands are `sweep`, `cleanup` and `verify`.

## Regression coverage

- `apps/web/e2e-upskii-production/harness.test.ts` covers the kill switch,
  QA-only addresses, the host and egress fences, the ledger fold, cleanup
  order and idempotency, purge looping, leak detection and the sweep's
  current-run protection.
- `scripts/ci/upskii-production-e2e-alert.test.mjs` covers the alert task
  lifecycle.
